title: Generated document review completion
target_user: An assigned reviewer completing a persisted generated-document review handoff
observed_problem: A reviewer can discover and re-download a pending generated-document packet, but cannot record a terminal review outcome that remains bound to that packet.

evidence.observation: The current product loop includes pending sign-off, completed-review validation, and final package export as consecutive steps.
The persisted generated-document reviewer handoff is explicitly limited to pending records and excludes review completion.
The existing slice treats completion decisions as a non-goal and ends after verified packet discovery and re-download.
The public surface exposes prepare, inbox, project history, and packet download routes but no completion route.
The generated-document review request schema currently defines creation input only.

current_workaround: The reviewer downloads the packet and communicates a decision outside DecisionDoc, while the persisted handoff remains pending and cannot provide packet-bound completion evidence.
desired_outcome: The assigned reviewer records one inspectable accepted, changes-requested, or rejected outcome and receives deterministic reviewed evidence without granting operational approval.
acceptance_criteria: Only the current session-bound stable assignee can complete a pending review; API keys, Ops keys, sessionless JWTs, viewers, and foreign users are rejected before mutation.
Completion requires the persisted packet and source document to remain current; changed or missing source state preserves the pending record and requires a new handoff.
One operation identity can move a record from pending to completed exactly once; an exact retry returns the same verified result and changed input is rejected.

The reviewed-evidence package deterministically binds the unchanged source packet, source SHA-256, tenant, project, document, stable reviewer identity, decision, rationale, review time, and receipt SHA-256.
Stored and returned records are independently revalidated; malformed, duplicate, foreign, missing, or hash-drifted state fails closed without rewriting source bytes.

Inbox and project history expose safe completed-review summaries and verified reviewed-package download while keeping rationale, stable identity, session, token, IP, and User-Agent out of list responses and audit details.
The browser completion action is single-flight and discards stale auth, tenant, user, project, document, request, packet, and operation responses before changing UI state or creating a download.
Every completion record, response, header, and reviewed package keeps approval, operational approval, provider, G2B, training, deployment, publication, bid, legal, and contractual authority false.
affected_boundaries: generated-document review tests and product documentation

allowed_effects: persist one terminal review-evidence transition for an existing generated-document review record
write one immutable reviewed-evidence package bound to the existing packet
append one redacted generated-document review audit event
excluded_effects: grant approval, legal, contractual, bid, or operational authority
call providers, G2B, OCR, transcription, training, or model APIs
deploy, publish, or mutate production infrastructure
reassign, notify, expire, delete, or garbage-collect review records
separate_approval_required_for: live AWS or S3 runtime verification
bid submission, legal approval, or contractual commitment

local_verification.proves: The exact candidate record is structurally valid and explicitly approved before implementation starts.
Local and fake-S3 record transitions, packet binding, authorization, replay, corruption, and API behavior are covered.
Browser contracts, app wiring, module boundaries, and false-authority surfaces remain explicit.
The real local browser flow handles completion, stale contexts, verified download, responsive layout, and client errors.
The completed feature preserves the repository-wide no-cost regression baseline.
Tracked product documentation and the portfolio mirror remain byte-consistent.

decision.rationale: The repository evidence demonstrates a bounded core review-loop gap, and the operator approved this exact local and fake-S3 implementation scope while retaining every external and operational exclusion.
